definitions.explanation: To sit or mount something with one leg on each side.
To extend over or across a boundary, area, or period of time.

examples.japanese: {自転車|じてんしゃ}に{跨|また}がって{出発|しゅっぱつ}した。
examples.english: I got on the bicycle and set off.

examples.japanese: バイクに{跨|また}がったまま{信号|しんごう}を{待|ま}っていた。
examples.english: I waited at the traffic light while still straddling the motorcycle.

examples.japanese: {二|ふた}つの{県|けん}に{跨|また}がる。
{工事|こうじ}は{三|さん}か{月|げつ}に{跨|また}がった。
このプロジェクトは{複数|ふくすう}の{部署|ぶしょ}に{跨|また}がる{大規模|だいきぼ}なものだ。
examples.english: This project is a large-scale one that spans multiple departments.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive). Pattern: Xに{跨|また}がる.

USAGE:
Sense 1 takes the particle に to mark what is being straddled. Sense 2 also uses に to mark the range or boundary being spanned. Both senses share the core meaning of extending across something.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{馬|うま}に{跨|また}がる (to mount a horse)
・{自転車|じてんしゃ}に{跨|また}がる (to get on a bicycle)
・{国境|こっきょう}に{跨|また}がる (to span a national border)
・{複数|ふくすう}の{分野|ぶんや}に{跨|また}がる (to span multiple fields)
